subject: Tri-zone handoff & load rehearsal — scheduling windows and prompt review
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Anna Shelby <anna.shelby@nimbusretail.com>, Miguel Torres <m.torres@nimbusretail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 21 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Tri-zone handoff & load rehearsal — scheduling windows and prompt review

Hi Anna / Miguel —

Thanks again for committing to the POC next week. To make the hands-on deep dives productive for both teams, proposed plan below:

1) Objective: run two full hands-on sessions (prompt tuning + routing validation) and one load rehearsal (simulated peak traffic) across US/EU/APAC.
2) Duration: 2.5 hours per session (tech intro + prompts walkthrough + live tests + retrospective).
3) Rolling windows (we want rotating start times so Redwood & Nimbus engineers overlap):
   - US window: 2027-03-29 08:00–10:30 PDT
   - EU window: 2027-03-29 15:00–17:30 CEST
   - APAC window: 2027-03-30 02:00–04:30 SGT (late; can shift earlier if needed)

Attached: nimbus_poc_milestones.xlsx (high-level agenda) and load_rehearsal_checklist.pdf (ops checklist).

Requests:
- Please confirm 1–2 preferred windows for your engineering leads (we can rotate so Redwood covers second half of APAC window).
- Share the short list of test prompts you want validated (max 10). We’ll prepare a prompt-review doc and run routing smoke tests.
- If you need IP whitelisting or a VPN tunnel, please send the contact and we’ll share IT instructions (see IT whitelist template attached).

Next steps: if Anna/Miguel confirm availability by EOD Monday, I’ll send calendar invites and a short runbook to all participants.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this scheduled.

Jonas Weber
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments: nimbus_poc_milestones.xlsx, load_rehearsal_checklist.pdf

Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 11:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Tri-zone handoff & load rehearsal — scheduling windows and prompt review

Thanks Jonas —

Those windows look reasonable. A couple of notes from our side:
- Our platform engineering lead (Miguel) prefers the EU window or a US late-morning slot; APAC at 02:00 SGT will be painful for our Singapore offshore team. Can we shift APAC to 23:00 SGT (previous day) instead?
- We have a hard constraint on Wednesday evenings (North America) due to retail batch processes — please avoid 03/31 21:00–23:00 PDT.
- I’ve attached our IT whitelist request form; our security team will need the Redwood ingress IPs and the planned test dates.

I’ll collect the engineering names and preferred times and circle back by tomorrow lunch. For prompt review: we’ll send a short bundle of 6 canonical prompts (customer-facing, multi-turn) that we want routing and safety checks run against.

Anna Shelby
Head of ML Integrations | Nimbus Retail
anna.shelby@nimbusretail.com

Date: Tue, 23 Mar 2027 08:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Tri-zone handoff & load rehearsal — scheduling windows and prompt review

Anna — appreciate the constraints. Quick internal update and proposal:

- APAC shift: we can move APAC to 2027-03-30 23:00–01:30 SGT (i.e., slightly earlier local time) which should be tolerable for our APAC on-call.
- To cover overlapping coverage we propose a rotating cadence across three sessions:
  * Session A (US-first): US lead 08:00–10:30 PDT; EU joins at 11:00 CET; APAC joins late.
  * Session B (EU-first): EU lead 14:00–16:30 CEST; US joins 05:00 PDT; APAC overlaps for final hour.
  * Session C (APAC-first): APAC lead 23:00–01:30 SGT; US team covers final hour for handoff notes.

Operational asks for the load rehearsal:
- We’ll run three ramp phases: low (10 rps), medium (50 rps), peak (150 rps) for 20 minutes each. Please confirm expected average prompt length (tokens) so we can size KV cache warmup and batch policies.
- We recommend a 15-minute KV-cache warmup before the peak run. We’ll include explicit routing smoke-test cases in the runbook.

I’ll create calendar placeholders once Anna confirms final participant list. Dylan will own the load scripts and will need access to your test endpoints by Monday EOD.

Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Manager | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Anna Shelby <anna.shelby@nimbusretail.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 24 Mar 2027 09:34:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Tri-zone handoff & load rehearsal — scheduling windows and prompt review

Looping in technical items from infra:

- Instance profile: for the peak run we recommend reserving a dedicated pool equivalent to 8xA100 (or 12 x A40) for the 90-minute peak window to avoid noisy neighbor impact. If Nimbus cannot provision that, we’ll fallback to an autoscaled dedicated tier but expect ~20% higher tail latency.
- KV-cache warmup: run a prefix replay for ~15 mins targeting 10k unique prefixes to populate the cache for routing tests. We’ll provide a small warmup generator script (Dylan will attach).
- Routing tests: ensure the test endpoints include both the canary model variant and the primary model. We’ll do A/B traffic split 10/90 during smoke tests and then 50/50 for one medium run.

Action items for Nimbus: share expected average prompt token size and a list of the 6 canonical prompts by EOD today.

Karthik Iyer
Lead Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Tri-zone handoff & load rehearsal — scheduling windows and prompt review

Anna / team — thanks for the quick replies and for the IT form. Finalized plan below based on constraints and internal checks:

Scheduled sessions (calendar invites to follow):
- Session 1 (EU-first walkthrough): 2027-03-29 15:00–17:30 CEST — prompt review + routing smoke tests
- Session 2 (US-first load run): 2027-03-30 08:00–10:30 PDT — ramped load (low/med/peak) with KV warmup at 07:45 PDT
- Session 3 (APAC handoff & retrospective): 2027-03-30 23:00–01:30 SGT — final prompt validations and runbook signoff

Runbook & prep items (we’ll publish a short runbook to the shared Drive):
- Dylan will attach the warmup generator and load scripts to the Drive folder by EOD.
- Karthik will reserve the dedicated node pool for the US-first load run; fallback policy will be autoscale with throttling rules.
- Anna: please confirm participant list and token-size estimate; also ensure your infra team fills the IT whitelist request (we received it).

Fallbacks: If the reserved pool cannot be confirmed, we will lower peak target to 100 rps and add an extra medium run to validate scaling behavior.

I’ll send calendar invites and include short pre-reads. Thanks everyone — looking forward to a smooth rehearsal.

Jonas Weber
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
